turns.text: Hey guys, Dylan from the Smart Economy podcast. We're at day 2 at Consensus 2024 here in Austin, Texas, and I'm chatting with Sergey Vasilchuk, the CEO, co-founder, you name it, at EverStake. How's it going, Sergey?
Yeah, nice to meet you guys. I'm fine. Good time, good market. Happy to see you.

So yesterday we got to catch up a little bit, and it was awesome. You recognized my name tag because of the Neo News Today stuff, but basically EverStake secures a ton of different blockchain networks. So for anyone who's never heard of what you guys do and who you are, what's like your elevator pitch? What do you do, and what networks do you secure?

So, like, we secure basically all the proof-of-stake blockchains. And, like, our goal is to make it sustainable, fast, and we just sign your transactions. Whatever transaction you sign, we're like most of the blockchains. There is a very high probability that we're the guy who signed your transaction. So we're technically your gateway to the blockchain.
And does it need to be proof-of-stake? Because we're starting to enter a world where there's, like, various different types of validator models, and maybe that is within or outside of your purview.

Like, it depends. Like, if you see, like, we support like 100 of the blockchains. I suppose, like, I hope that we'll be like another 200, and each of them will find a specific niche. So the way how and the reason why we started the EverStake, because I was thinking and assuming that in order to be fast, fast enough, we need to have the professional validators, professional parties, like, to make a great job.
Yeah.
And, like, my bet wasright. And for the most of the, like, DeFi or fast-performing blockchains, like, we really need the validators.

Yes. So I think what's super cool about EverStake is whenever I'm trying out a new blockchain ecosystem, I have a name that I can trust when I want to stake and validate. So what are your kind of criteria for which blockchains? Because you guys support 100 blockchains, but there are thousands of them. So what do you look for in a new blockchain ecosystem when you want to provide validation services?

Well, like, our credo, like, is to be useful. So, like, we have some expertise, like, in many of the fields. Unfortunately, another, like, 200 of the blockchains were already dead. But they went from our hands, and, like, at least we know what not to do.
Right.

And, like, we have this, like, gut feeling already. And, like, of course we have some, like, research and scientific, like, approach. But, like, gut feelings, like, also tell us, like, what, like, chains we need to select, what not, what to skip. And, like, it's simple, less like ABC. Like, if we find the way to be useful there, like, we join. If not, like, we cannot, like, be everywhere.

So the more education we're doing, like, the better, like, for us, for our customers, and for the global community. So it's tough. It's a long way. But, like, it's payoff.

Well, the good news for us and, like, the community in total, that, like, we have the rise of the, like, up chain.
